audit.why: 56.63% over 4863 games and an all-Fizz chart agree across both layers and the packet. Lux has no dash and no self-peel beyond a shield, so every row stays Fizz; difficulty 4/10 holds.
audit.corrected: Chart untouched; the whys were reworded only where they carried a wrong ability name.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content claimed Playful/Trickster 'nulls the whole ultimate' and referred to 'Prism block' and 'Shield' as if they were separate abilities.
audit.why: Final Spark is 60/50/40 and Riot's text says 'After gathering energy, Lux fires a beam' — the gather is the tell, and the untargetable frame takes you out of the beam; claiming the whole ultimate is nullified is a magnitude with no source. Her W is Prismatic Barrier, a 1150-range shield, and there is no ability called Prism.
audit.corrected: spikes[1], spikes[2], spikes[3], mid and late rewritten with real names and the 60s / flat 10s numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two interactions that decide the lane were only gestured at: Light Binding binds a limited number of units, and Illumination is an auto-attack payoff.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Lux releases a sphere of light that binds and deals damage to up to two enemy units' at 1175 on a flat 10s — a minion in the line eats it. Illumination charges the target on any damaging spell and her next basic attack ignites it, so her auto wind-up, not her cast, is the cue. Lucent Singularity (1100, 10/9.5/9/8.5/8) is the slow zone; Prismatic Barrier (1150) is the shield.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns, dos/donts and spikes now state the two-unit cap, the flat 10s, the passive auto tell and the shield range.

audit.why: The packet's suspectNames hit on 'Her Final Spark' is a false positive — Final Spark is Lux's real R name and was left in place.
